judge_assessment.explanation: The first hard failure is fully supported. The directions state in bold 'On every problem, name the method you chose before you compute', the answer key answers every problem by opening with 'Method: ...', and verify.json holds ten entries -- all triangle, eval or approx with a numeric or ratio expected -- and not one manual entry. The method name is a required printed response on all ten problems and is recorded on none, so the sheet reports as fully machine-verified while the skill the prompt names ('choosing among Pythagorean, special-triangle, and trig methods') is entirely outside the trust boundary. That alone is a hard failure under the rubric. The second hard failure is wrong on its facts. I read worksheet.tex directly: problem 6 is '\problem[6cm]{Find the length of side $a$. Give an exact answer --- this one needs no calculator.}' -- there is no request for a one-sentence justification anywhere in it, and none in the compiled PDF. Problem 10 is '\textbf{Challenge.} The triangle below is isosceles, not right angled. Find the measure of each base angle. Hint: the height from C to side c splits it into two congruent right triangles --- decide which method fits one of those.' -- a hint, not a request for a written explanation. The judge invented two specific citations to support a conclusion that is already true on other grounds, and citing evidence that is not in the artifact weakens a correct verdict. Independently, all ten values recompute: 10, 9.90, 6.30, 12, 22.62, 6, 8/15, 13, 7.07, 53.13, and the figure givens match the JSON. REJECT stands.

strengths_to_preserve: The interleave is genuinely method-driven and the givens do the work, not the wording. Consecutive problems never call for the same tool -- Pythagorean, special triangle, trig, Pythagorean, trig, special triangle, ratio, Pythagorean, special triangle, trig -- and each item is distinguished only by what is supplied (two sides, a 30/45-degree angle, or an arbitrary angle). A student cannot pattern-match on phrasing.

Every problem carries its own to-scale figure generated by scripts/render_figures.py from the same verified JSON the key uses, so a figure cannot disagree with its answer. Judge visual review confirmed all ten render unclipped across seven pages.

Problem 10 is a real synthesis item rather than a harder instance of problem 9: the triangle is deliberately NOT right-angled, so the student has to manufacture a right triangle (drop the altitude, halve the base to 6) before any of the sheet's three methods becomes applicable. The prompt asked the sheet to 'finish with one synthesis challenge appropriate to the level' and this is one.

Seven of the ten problems declare a trap keyed to the specific wrong method rather than to arithmetic slips -- 'used sine instead of tangent, dividing by the hypotenuse the problem never gave' (5.16), 'added the squares instead of subtracting' (17.49), 'used the 30-60-90 ratio the wrong way round' (10.39), 'halved the diagonal instead of using the 45-45-90 ratio' (5). These are method-choice errors, which is exactly what the sheet assesses.

root_causes.description: A required response that is a WORD ('Pythagorean theorem', 'special triangle', 'trig ratio') has no representable form. Every verify type produces a number; `manual` exists but the author read it as reserved for open reasoning, and a method name from a closed three-item vocabulary does not feel open. With no entry kind that fits, the requirement stated in bold in the directions and answered at the top of every key solution was declared nowhere.
evidence: worksheet.tex line 26: '\textbf{On every problem, name the method you chose before you compute}'
answer_key.pdf: every solution begins 'Method: Pythagorean theorem' / 'Method: special triangle (30-60-90)' / 'Method: definition of the ratio'
verify.json: ten entries, types triangle/eval/approx, no manual entry anywhere in the file
machine observation: gate_chain_manual_flags false -- the build reports zero manual items

root_causes.description: The task contract sets review_mode 'machine_first' with verification_targets ['approx','triangle','eval'] -- no 'manual' target -- which reads as a signal that this case should have no manual items. The author produced exactly that and was then hard-failed for it. The contract and the rubric's 'an open proof, construction, graph, or explanation is falsely described as machine-verified' rule point in opposite directions when a sheet's directions demand a named method.
evidence: task_contract.verification_targets: ['approx', 'triangle', 'eval'] with review_mode 'machine_first' -- 'manual' absent, unlike the other nine cases in my batch
final_response.md and gate_log.txt report a clean exit-0-style pass with no manual items
rubric.md hard failure: 'An open proof, construction, graph, or explanation is falsely described as machine-verified'

improvements.title: The named method required on every problem must carry a manual entry
improvements.proposed_change: State in SKILL.md that a required NAMED CHOICE -- method, theorem, angle-pair, rule -- is a response slot in its own right and takes a `manual` entry under the same id, with the expected name in `desc`, even when the vocabulary is closed and even when the sheet is otherwise machine-first. Enforce it in scripts/verify.py by scanning the directions block and each problem segment for naming imperatives ('name the method', 'name the theorem', 'state which', 'say which rule') and exiting 2 listing every id with no manual entry. On curr-325 that fires on all ten ids and would have surfaced before delivery, because the requirement is stated once in the shared directions rather than per problem -- which is precisely why it was overlooked.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture whose directions block reads 'On every problem, name the method you chose before you compute' and whose verify JSON contains only triangle entries; assert verify.py exits 2 and lists every problem id. It exits 0 today because each id has a numeric check.
improvements.expected_impact: Puts the sheet's declared focus inside the trust boundary. Method selection is the whole point of an interleaved-synthesis review; today it is the one thing not recorded anywhere in the verification data.
improvements.risk: Medium. Firing on all ten ids of a sheet whose directions carry a blanket instruction is correct but loud; it also collides with review_mode 'machine_first', so the message should say plainly that a manual item is the required outcome here, not a defect.

improvements.title: machine_first contracts should not imply zero manual items when the sheet requires a named choice
improvements.proposed_change: Make the relationship explicit in rubric.md and in the suite's task contracts: verification_targets lists the machine CHECK KINDS a case is expected to use and never forbids a `manual` entry; review_mode 'machine_first' means machine checks are preferred where a response is computable, not that the sheet must report zero manual items. Add a sentence to rubric.md's hard-failure list making that reading explicit, so an author writing to a machine_first contract does not read the absence of 'manual' from verification_targets as a prohibition.
improvements.regression_test: Add a suite-level assertion in tests/test_curriculum_eval_suite.py that no task contract whose worksheet directions require a named choice can be satisfied with zero manual entries -- i.e. that a machine_first fixture with a naming directive and no manual entry is reported as a coverage failure rather than a clean pass. Today such a case passes cleanly.
improvements.expected_impact: Removes a contradiction that punishes an author for following the contract. Any machine_first case in the suite whose sheet asks for a named method, theorem or rule is exposed to the same trap.
improvements.risk: Low. This is documentation plus one suite-level assertion; it changes no generated artifact and no gate behaviour for existing passing cases.

case_summary: The right-triangle mathematics is correct throughout (10, 9.90, 6.30, 12, 22.62 degrees, 6, tan A = 8/15, 13 ft, 7.07 cm, 53.13 degrees), the interleave is genuinely method-driven with no two consecutive problems taking the same tool, every figure is generated from the same verified JSON the key uses, and problem 10 is a real synthesis item that forces the student to manufacture a right triangle before any method applies. The rejection is right on its first ground: the directions demand in bold that the student name the chosen method on every problem, the key answers every problem with 'Method: ...', and verify.json contains ten numeric entries and zero manual entries, so the declared focus -- method selection -- sits entirely outside verification. The judge's second hard failure is not supported by the artifacts: I checked worksheet.tex line by line and problem 6 reads only 'Find the length of side a. Give an exact answer' with no justification request, and problem 10's 'decide which method fits one of those' is a hint, not a request for a written explanation. A contributing factor worth recording: this is the only case in my batch whose contract omits 'manual' from verification_targets and sets review_mode machine_first, which reads as an instruction to produce exactly the zero-manual sheet that was then hard-failed.
